title: Prior versus case-evidence weighting
description: Whether reasoning is represented as anchored more strongly to a registered base rate or as responsive more strongly to case-specific evidence, without identifying evidence polarity or diagnosticity as the construct.

contrast_conditions.label: Prior/base-rate sensitive
contrast_conditions.definition: The reasoning state preserves and gives substantial weight to the base rate or prior probability when interpreting a new case.

contrast_conditions.label: Case-evidence sensitive
contrast_conditions.definition: The reasoning state gives substantial weight to case-specific evidence when interpreting a new case, relative to the registered base rate.

probe_prompt_template:
Read the following short reasoning scenario. Track how the base rate and case-specific evidence are weighted separately from whether the evidence supports or contradicts the hypothesis.

Scenario:
{scenario}

Continue processing the scenario.

independent_behavior_task.prompt_template: In a separate probability judgment, start with the stated prior probability and then consider one case-specific result whose evidential force is fixed at the registered moderate level. Report the posterior probability from 0 to 100 as one integer. Use only the numbers and evidence described in this item.
independence_requirements: Use new hypotheses, domains, entities, and evidence items not present in probe prompts.
Cross low, middle, and high priors with supporting and contradicting evidence.
Hold case-evidence force at the registered moderate level; do not vary diagnosticity, reliability, specificity, or noise.
Do not ask the model to label the reasoning style or to repeat the probe scenario.

expected_by_evidence_strength.moderate: prior_sensitive produces a smaller posterior distance from the stated prior than case_evidence_sensitive

behavior.warning: This construct concerns relative prior-versus-case weighting, not evidence diagnosticity, evidence polarity, or calibration quality alone.

metadata.primary_question: Does a prior-versus-case weighting direction transfer to posterior judgments in new domains?
